chapter: GK: Space and the Natural World
trick: Sort the planets by what makes each one famous rather than by name alone: the hottest is Venus, the largest is Jupiter, the red one is Mars, the ringed one is Saturn. Examiners ask for the superlative, so learn the superlatives.

video.query: solar system planets facts largest hottest general knowledge for students

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement about space and the natural world.

items.statement: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system.
items.why: It is bigger than all the other planets put together, and its Great Red Spot is a storm wider than the Earth.

items.statement: Mercury is the hottest planet because it is nearest the Sun.
items.why: Venus is hotter. Its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, while Mercury has almost no atmosphere to hold any.
It is an ordinary star that only looks different because it is so much nearer to us than the rest.

items.statement: Light from the Sun reaches the Earth in about eight minutes.
items.why: The Sun is about 150 million kilometres away and light travels 300,000 kilometres a second.

items.statement: The Moon makes its own light.
items.why: The Moon only reflects sunlight, which is why we see phases as the lit half turns towards or away from us.

chapter: GK: Indian National Symbols and Personalities
trick: The two commonest traps are a pair each. Bird is the peacock but animal is the tiger; the anthem is Jana Gana Mana but the song is Vande Mataram. Learn them as pairs and the questions stop being able to catch you.

video.query: national symbols of India list bird animal flower song anthem

data.prompt: Complete the list of national symbols. Two words in the bank are decoys.
data.text: The national bird of India is the {1} and the national animal is the {2}. The national flower is the {3} and the national fruit is the {4}. The national anthem is {5}, written by Rabindranath Tagore, while the national song is {6}, written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.

trick: Before you answer, ask whether the superlative is Indian or worldwide. The longest river in India is the Ganga, in the world the Nile; the highest peak in India is Kangchenjunga, in the world Everest. Same question, two answers.

data.prompt: Is each superlative true of India or of the world? Sort them.

items.label: The Ganga is the longest river
The Nile is the longest river
Mount Everest is the highest peak
The Thar is the largest desert
The Sahara is the largest hot desert
Rajasthan is the largest state by area
Russia is the largest country by area

trick: Most of these questions are really headquarters questions. Learn the city with the body: New York for the UN, Paris for UNESCO, Geneva for the WHO, Washington for the World Bank and the IMF. The odd one out is the International Court of Justice, at The Hague.
